native_statement.reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive-group structure and its Borel measurable-space structure, including the case dim(E)=0. Let V:E->R be C2. Let alpha,beta be nonnegative real numbers and eta a real number. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, eta>0, beta*eta<=1, and, for every x,v in E, alpha*||v||^2 <= D(DV)(x)[v][v] <= beta*||v||^2. Define mu as the normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume by -V. Define J as the pushforward of mu times the standard Gaussian on E under (a,z)->(a,a+sqrt(eta) z). Define nu as the second marginal of J. Define Lambda as the pushforward of J under (a,y)->(y,2a-y). Then mu,J,nu are probability measures. There exists a Markov kernel S:E->Measure(E) such that, for every y in E, S(y) is the normalized volume tilt with log weight x->-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta); S is a conditional kernel for Lambda, and both marginals of Lambda equal nu. For this same S there exists a bounded continuous real-linear operator T on H=L^2(nu;R) such that T is selfadjoint; for every u in H, ||Tu||<=||u||, the function representing Tu equals y->integral u(x) S(y)(dx) for nu-almost every y, and integral Tu dnu=integral u dnu. The operator D=I-(T composed with T) is positive. There exists a bounded continuous real-linear positive operator Gamma:H->H such that Gamma composed with Gamma=D and, for every u in H, ||Gamma u||^2=||u||^2-||Tu||^2. Furthermore, for every bounded continuous real-linear operator Gamma' on this same H, positivity of Gamma' and Gamma' composed with Gamma'=D imply Gamma'=Gamma.

native_statement.domains: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space; volume is its canonical measure, and stdGaussian E is the standard Gaussian on E. V is real-valued and twice continuously Frechet differentiable on all E. alpha and beta are of type nonnegative real, coerced to real in inequalities. eta is real. H=L2(nu;R) consists of almost-everywhere classes, is complete, and need not be finite-dimensional even though E is. Every operator in the conclusion and every alternative Gamma' has precisely domain and codomain H with the same actual measure nu.
native_statement.quantifiers: Universally quantify all displayed ambient data and hypotheses. The Hessian condition quantifies globally over both x and v. After the four local measure definitions, probability of mu AND probability of J AND probability of nu AND the existence of S hold together. Inside existence of S, all its kernel/disintegration/marginal claims hold AND there exists T. Inside existence of T, its operator/action/mean/defect claims hold AND there exists Gamma. Inside existence of Gamma, positivity AND exact square AND every-u energy equality AND every-Gamma' uniqueness hold together. The alternative-root quantifier is outside the preceding every-u energy quantifier; it is not indexed by u and it does not assume an energy identity for Gamma'.

native_statement.scopes: For every y, equality S(y)=tilted(volume, log_weight_y) is equality of measures at every state, including states outside any nu-full set; its normalizing constant may depend on y. In contrast, the integral action formula for T is stated separately for each observable u as equality nu-almost everywhere, allowing the exceptional set to depend on u. It does not claim one common exceptional set for all observables, nor pointwise action at every y for arbitrary representatives. Norm, mean and energy statements quantify over every L2 equivalence class. Lambda.IsCondKernel S describes disintegration of the second coordinate given the first: Lambda is obtained from its first marginal nu and S; both marginals are nu. Products A*B mean composition, so T*T is T squared, I is the identity bounded operator and the defect is I-T^2. Since T is selfadjoint, its displayed defect/energy relation has the form associated with I-T* T, but the exact statement uses T*T and supplies selfadjointness separately. Gamma and Gamma' are bounded positive operators with the identical square D. Only Gamma is given the energy certificate. Alternative-root uniqueness requires only positivity and exact square for Gamma', with conclusion equality of operators.
